__diagram__.text: This view is a proposed design; it is not current behavior. Skills orchestrate public Ply commands and explain public results. They cannot parse ply.lock, construct VisualEnvelope files, weaken intent silently, or become a second verifier.

skills-verify.text: The skill may repair implementation code and rerun Ply. It stops for developer approval before changing architecture intent, contracts, declared checks, or evidence requirements.

skills-cli.text: Atomic publication, discovery, retention, cleanup, fingerprints, verdicts, and SVG generation remain implemented and enforced by Ply core and its CLI.

designs.name: Publish a portable validated Ply visual envelope
designs.goal: Turn declared intent and earned evidence into one editor-neutral visual snapshot without duplicating Ply semantics in clients
nonGoals: Running verification from an IDE automatically
Moving evidence interpretation into JavaScript or Kotlin
Forking the existing visual grammar into each client
constraints: Ply core remains the only authority on verdict and evidence meaning
A client never reads ply.lock or combines Ply inputs itself
The envelope is strict, versioned, offline-capable, and safe to treat as untrusted workspace data
Every grammar construct retains one drawable meaning

decisions.text: Keep hierarchy, stable identity, evidence state, diagnostics, and source mappings in Rust
decisions.rationale: Every client must show the same result without becoming a second verifier

decisions.text: Extract and extend the existing Rust SVG renderer instead of forking it
decisions.rationale: One visual grammar prevents drift across static reports and IDEs

decisions.text: Let the LLM manage Ply execution and publish immutable visual runs
decisions.rationale: IDEs remain inexpensive observers and do not surprise developers with verification work

decisions.text: Describe each view as a specific completed run rather than tracking later source edits
decisions.rationale: Ply decides reuse and validity on the next run; clients need no duplicate fingerprint logic

decisions.text: Publish immutable runs under target/ply/views/<run-id>/visual.json and atomically replace target/ply/view.json as their index
decisions.rationale: target/ply is already Ply-owned, disposable, and independent of IDE implementation

decisions.text: Publish a visual run only when the LLM requests it through an explicit verify option
decisions.rationale: Existing verification and CI workflows do not acquire an unrequested artifact side effect

decisions.text: Retain the latest 20 completed runs per Ply root by default and clean them through a core-owned command
decisions.rationale: Run comparison remains useful without unbounded storage growth or client-specific cleanup

decisions.text: Publish one independent visual index for each directory containing ply.yaml
decisions.rationale: Clients can select roots without merging evidence across separately verified scopes

assumptions: The current renderer can be extracted behind a stable Rust interface without changing the grammar
The existing result envelope and ply.lock record contain the evidence required by the visual model

acceptanceCriteria.text: Rust tests pin VisualEnvelope compatibility, stable element IDs, exact source mappings, and strict rejection of unknown major versions
Static SVG and published visual artifacts use the same renderer and visual vocabulary
Interrupted publication cannot replace a complete discoverable artifact with a partial one
Publication retains at most the configured number of completed runs and never removes the run referenced by the current index
Adversarial labels, contracts, diagnostics, and source paths cannot inject script or external content into generated SVG

plan.text: Extract the current SVG and layout implementation behind a reusable Rust visual module
Define VisualEnvelope with protocol version, SVG, semantic element metadata, evidence, diagnostics, run identity, and exact source locations
Add explicit --publish-view output, atomic target/ply run indexing, per-root discovery, bounded retention, and cleanup to the LLM-facing CLI workflow

designs.name: Build the shared Ply visual application
designs.goal: Provide one browser-based navigation and evidence experience that behaves identically in standalone Chromium, VS Code, and JetBrains
nonGoals: Reading Ply source files or result records
Running verification
Graphically editing the specification in the first release
Integrating with a specific LLM vendor
constraints: The same compiled viewer assets run in Chromium, VS Code webviews, and JetBrains JCEF
Declared intent and earned evidence share one canvas
Colour never carries evidence meaning alone
The viewer runs offline and treats the envelope as untrusted data

decisions.text: Own the shared visual application as packages/ply-vis inside the ply-vis client monorepo
decisions.rationale: Neither IDE becomes the reference implementation, and both adapters consume one package in the same repository

decisions.text: Combine physical zoom with semantic focus from workspace through component, function, contract, evidence, and counterexample
decisions.rationale: Developers can scan broadly and inspect narrowly without switching diagram products

decisions.text: Use a small versioned host bridge for exact source navigation, state persistence, artifact requests, readiness, and errors
decisions.rationale: Host-specific APIs remain outside the visual application

decisions.text: Distribute pinned compiled assets to hosts at build time
decisions.rationale: The viewer stays reproducible, secure, and offline

assumptions: VS Code webviews and JetBrains JCEF expose the browser features required by the shared viewer
The Rust envelope provides all semantic information needed for inspection

acceptanceCriteria.text: Headless Playwright covers boot, zoom, pan, fit, semantic focus, selection, inspection, host messages, state restoration, malformed envelopes, and runtime errors
A fixture with 500 components and 5,000 functions opens its workspace view within two seconds and remains responsive through semantic focus
Keyboard navigation, visible focus, semantic labels, colour-independent states, text scaling, and reduced motion are tested
CSP forbids injected scripts, eval, and external resources; malformed or incompatible envelopes retain the last good snapshot with a clear error

plan.text: Create the editor-neutral application shell, strict envelope parser, immutable view state, CSP, and host bridge
Embed the Rust SVG, add zoom, focus, selection, evidence inspection, run selection, and exact source requests
Port the useful Archi-Techture browser test pattern and add Ply-specific behavioral and security fixtures

decisions.text: Watch complete LLM-published artifacts and host ply-vis without automatic verification

designs.name: Orchestrate Ply through portable LLM skills
designs.goal: Make verification and evidence review routine for implementation agents without moving Ply authority into prompts
nonGoals: Constructing or editing VisualEnvelope artifacts
Parsing ply.lock
Reimplementing fingerprint, verdict, retention, or discovery rules
Silently weakening architecture, contracts, checks, or evidence requirements
Binding the workflow to a single LLM vendor
constraints: Skills invoke only documented public Ply commands and consume public output
Ply core remains the sole writer of visual artifacts and the sole authority on evidence meaning
An implementation agent invokes verification after changing code covered by ply.yaml and before claiming completion
Every completed result is publishable, including violations, narrowed coverage, and missing evidence

decisions.text: Ship separate ply-verify and ply-review skills
decisions.rationale: Running and repairing a verification loop is distinct from explaining a completed run to a developer

decisions.text: Allow implementation repair but require developer approval before any spec-level weakening
decisions.rationale: An agent may fix code to meet intent; it may not redefine success to obtain green output

decisions.text: Keep canonical tool-neutral SKILL.md sources in the Ply repository with thin installer metadata for supported agents
decisions.rationale: The workflow has one authoritative representation and remains portable

decisions.text: Require skills to request artifact publication from Ply rather than writing files themselves
decisions.rationale: Atomicity, compatibility, evidence semantics, and retention stay machine-enforced

assumptions: Supported agents can execute local commands and read structured public output
A portable SKILL.md can express the common workflow while installer metadata handles agent-specific discovery

acceptanceCriteria.text: ply-verify handles clean, violation with counterexample, missing evidence, narrowed coverage, timeout, and internal-tool-error fixtures without misreporting completion
ply-review explains declared intent, earned evidence, assumptions, gaps, run identity, and exact source links from public output without reading private records
Scenario tests prove the skills stop for approval before weakening a contract, architecture rule, declared check, or evidence requirement
The skills contain no artifact serializer, ply.lock parser, verdict classifier, retention logic, or IDE-specific integration
